summary: Lists common IANA allocations for mobile ad hoc network protocols. The needed well-known numbers are a UDP port number, an IP protocol number, and a link-local multicast group address, which many such protocols can share.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 5498 assigns shared UDP, IP protocol and multicast values for MANET protocols that use RFC 5444's common packet format. The common format lets interoperable protocols share these values without ambiguity.

subtitle: Shared IANA numbers for protocols that use the MANET packet format

tldr.problem: Protocols using the common MANET message format need shared well-known identifiers to send and receive packets.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC assigns a UDP port, an IP protocol number and link-local multicast addresses for MANET routers.
tldr.outcome: Protocols using these allocations MUST conform to RFC 5444 so they can share them unambiguously.

today: RFC 5498 is a Standards Track document that assigns shared IANA values for MANET protocols conforming to RFC 5444.

sections.title: Common Values for MANET Protocols
sections.content:
This document lists common IANA allocations for one or more Mobile Ad hoc Network (MANET) protocols that conform to RFC 5444. The required values are a UDP port number, an IP protocol number and a link-local multicast group address.

Interoperable protocols using these well-known allocations MUST conform to RFC 5444. The RFC says that shared packet format lets one or more protocols use the allocations unambiguously.
sections.plainLanguage: Protocols using this shared set of network numbers must follow RFC 5444's common packet format. That lets them use the same allocations without ambiguity.

sections.title: UDP, IP and Multicast Assignments
sections.content:
The assigned UDP port is 269, with the title manet. The assigned IP protocol number is 138, also titled manet.

The link-local multicast group is named LL-MANET-Routers. Its IPv4 address is 224.0.0.109 and its IPv6 address is FF02:0:0:0:0:0:0:6D.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC assigns one UDP port, one IP protocol number and a multicast address for each IP version. MANET routers use the allocations to send and receive routing packets.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC specifies only well-known numbers for protocols conforming to RFC 5444; it does not specify the protocols that carry information across the network. It says using these allocations does not affect the security issues of each protocol.

If multiple cooperating protocols share an allocation such as the UDP port, each protocol specification MUST address how their security policies interact.
sections.plainLanguage: The number assignments do not define protocol security. Each protocol that shares an allocation must explain how its security policy works with the others.
